problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. The available containers are:

* Container 1: volume 14 m³, revenue $23,000
* Container 2: volume 46 m³, revenue $242,000
* Container 3: volume 40 m³, revenue $98,000
* Container 4: volume 40 m³, revenue $236,000
* Container 5: volume 21 m³, revenue $177,000
* Container 6: volume 28 m³, revenue $300,000
* Container 7: volume 50 m³, revenue $83,000
* Container 8: volume 33 m³, revenue $229,000
* Container 9: volume 26 m³, revenue $131,000
* Container 10: volume 24 m³, revenue $205,000
* Container 11: volume 19 m³, revenue $133,000
* Container 12: volume 14 m³, revenue $140,000
* Container 13: volume 16 m³, revenue $284,000
* Container 14: volume 38 m³, revenue $200,000
* Container 15: volume 30 m³, revenue $131,000
* Container 16: volume 39 m³, revenue $182,000
* Container 17: volume 40 m³, revenue $84,000
* Container 18: volume 21 m³, revenue $134,000

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 377 m³. Determine which containers to load to maximize total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be loaded in its entirety or not at all.
